note: What the applicability screen asks and what it looks for. The screen decides one thing only: whether a legality, privacy or biosafety review by a person applies before anything is planned. It is not a judgement of the science and it does not understand a question; it catches what a requester declares and what a text names. Results: CLEAR (the standing approval rule objective-clear-screen may confirm it), NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW (it waits for a person), BLOCKED (no run is started). Changing this file changes its sha256, which every screen result records.

questions.text: Does the work use data about identifiable people: patient or medical records, a named person's genome, contact details?
Must private or unpublished data be sent to a service outside this machine?
Is the result meant to guide the diagnosis or treatment of a person?
Does the work need controlled or export-restricted material, or access the requester holds no licence for?
Does the work include making, culturing, modifying or releasing a biological agent, or a protocol for doing so?
Is the aim, or a foreseeable use of the result, to make a pathogen or toxin more harmful, more transmissible, harder to detect or harder to treat?
